turns.prompt_text: does the Google pixel 9 have lighter in the front facing camera or the back facing camera
turns.response_html:
The Google Pixel 9 has a physical LED flash on the back camera only.

The front-facing camera does not have a physical flash. Instead, it uses Selfie Illumination, a software feature that turns the phone's screen bright white to light up your face when taking photos or videos.

Actually, the Google Pixel 9 does not have a LiDAR sensor on either the front or the back.

While some competitors (like the iPhone Pro models) use LiDAR for 3D scanning and depth sensing, Google uses different technology for its camera features:

1. The Back Cameras: LDAF

Instead of LiDAR, the Pixel 9 uses LDAF (Laser Detect Auto-Focus).

  • Where it is: It is located on the back camera bar, usually seen as a small dark circle near the lenses.
  • What it does: It shoots a single laser beam to quickly measure the distance to an object. This helps the camera focus instantly, especially in low light, but it cannot "map" a room in 3D like LiDAR can.

2. The Front Camera: Dual PD

The front camera uses Dual PD (Phase Detection) auto-focus.

  • What it does: It uses pixels on the image sensor itself to calculate distance and focus. It provides enough depth data for "Portrait Mode" (blurring the background), but it is not a 3D scanner.

Note: If you see a small extra sensor on the back of a Pixel 9 Pro model, that is actually an Infrared Temperature Sensor (used for measuring the temperature of objects or people), not a depth-sensing LiDAR.

Are you looking to use the phone for 3D scanning or measuring objects? I can suggest some apps that use the Pixel's standard cameras to do that!

Since the Pixel 9 doesn't have a dedicated LiDAR sensor, it relies on Photogrammetry (using multiple photos to create a 3D model) and Google’s ARCore (software that uses the camera and motion sensors to track the floor and walls).

Based on insights from tech communities and specialized developers, here are the best ways to use your Pixel 9 for scanning and measuring:

1. Best 3D Scanning Apps (No LiDAR Required)

These apps are highly recommended by hobbyists and creators who use Android. They use the Pixel’s high-quality camera to piece together a 3D model from many angles.

  • Polycam (Top Choice): Very popular for its ease of use. You walk around an object, and it "stitches" the photos into a detailed 3D mesh. It also has a "Room Mode" for floor plans.
  • KIRI Engine: Frequently cited as the "best for Android" in 2025. It uses AI-driven photogrammetry and a new technology called 3D Gaussian Splatting, which makes textures look much more realistic than traditional scanning.
  • Widar: Great for people who want to edit the scan directly on their phone. It includes a full 3D editing suite.
  • RealityScan: Created by the makers of the Unreal Engine (Epic Games). It’s free and produces professional-grade models for game design or 3D printing.

2. Best Measuring & AR Apps

Because the Pixel 9 lacks LiDAR, measuring works best when you have good lighting and a textured surface (like a rug or wooden floor) for the camera to "grip" onto.

  • AR Ruler App: This is the most versatile "digital tape measure." It can calculate height, perimeter, and even the volume of 3D objects like boxes or cylinders.
  • AR Plan 3D: If you are trying to map a house, this app helps you "draw" a 3D floor plan by simply clicking on the corners of the room through your camera.
  • Magicplan: Widely used by real estate agents and contractors. It uses your camera to scan a room and create an instant CAD-style floor plan.

3. Pro-Tips for Success on Pixel 9

Since your phone uses software rather than a laser to "see" depth, follow these community-shared tips for better results:

  • Avoid Reflective Surfaces: The camera gets "confused" by glass, mirrors, or shiny metal because it can't tell where the surface ends.
  • Consistent Lighting: Don't scan in the dark. The Pixel’s LDAF (Laser Auto-Focus) will help focus, but the 3D software needs to see detail to map the object.
  • Slow, Steady Motion: When measuring or scanning, move the phone in a slow "painting" motion to let the ARCore software build a stable map of the environment.
